title: Xiaomi Mi Box S 2nd gen (model MiTV-AFKR0, codename jaws, Amlogic), Google TV / Android 11 (SDK 30),
notes:
Xiaomi Mi Box S 2nd gen (model MiTV-AFKR0, codename jaws, Amlogic), Google TV / Android 11 (SDK 30),
2 GB RAM. Fingerprints: Xiaomi/jaws/jaws:11/RTT0.211222.001/772:user/release-keys and
RTT0.211222.001.737 (validated 2026-10-19 on a Philco 4K TV)

Apply:   TV_HOST=<box ip> tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-box-s-2nd-gen/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<box ip> tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-box-s-2nd-gen/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. HOME claimants on stock: launcherx (priority 2),
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity (priority 1), Settings FallbackHome.
A streaming box: no HDMI-in or tuner, leave live_tv_package empty in config.xml; the Inputs pill hides itself.

Tested: every package below was disabled in batches with screenshots in between, the launcher from
launcher/ was installed and owns Home, and Home and Wi-Fi both came back by themselves after a reboot.
Validated again 2026-10-19 on 737: launcher com.gathin.tvhome owns Home,
cname switched from setupwraith to com.android.tv.settings and survives reboot. Still provisional
until few-days soak per CONTRIBUTING.md, but second confirmation.

Notes from this box:
- The stock adb on macOS connected fine on port 5555 once USB debugging was on; no wireless-debugging
pairing and no tools/tv.py needed.
- Disabling launcherx alone makes Home resolve to setupwraith's RecoveryActivity; `cmd package
set-home-activity` reports Success but does not take effect until setupwraith is disabled too.
- Right after disabling setupwraith, Wi-Fi dropped for about 20 seconds and the box asked for the Wi-Fi
password again. Once it was re-entered, it stayed saved across a reboot.
- After living with it: Wi-Fi, USB playback (with debugging off), Google Home, the phone remote,
Chromecast from a Pixel and Google Assistant all still work. On 737, display is 1920x1080 UI
with Settings > Tela e som > Resolução = 4k 60Hz (video 4K, HDR none on Philco 2016 EDID).
- The remote's shortcut buttons (Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Xiaomi TV+, Apps) all do nothing once
launcherx is disabled. Prime Video and Xiaomi TV+ are disabled anyway; Netflix, YouTube and Apps were
handled by launcherx, as on the Chromecast with Google TV (see that list for a Key Mapper remap).
The launcher brings them back: the Bluetooth remote ("Xiaomi RC", Vendor_2717_Product_32b9.kl) sends
Netflix as KEY_VIDEOPHONE -> 193 (BUTTON_6), YouTube as KEY_PRESENTATION -> 190 (BUTTON_3) and Prime
Video as KEY_PLAY -> 194 (BUTTON_7). app_keys 193:com.netflix.ninja, 190:<youtube app>,
194:<any app> with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh; checked on 737 with the real
remote (190 sent to SmartTube, 194 to Nuvio). The remote sleeps after a few seconds and drops the
first press that wakes it, so press OK before each button while reading them with getevent -lt.

Kept on purpose: Google Assistant (katniss), Chromecast (mediashell), phone remote (tv.remote.service),
YouTube Music, Xiaomi USB media apps (mimusic2, mitv.gallery, mediaexplorer, mitv.videoplayer),
Miracast (smartshare, wfdsinkhelperservice), com.xiaomi.tvqs.overseas (quick settings panel),
com.xiaomi.android.tvsetup.partnercustomizer (remote shortcut buttons - safe to disable if you don't
use the Netflix/YouTube/Prime shortcut keys; tested disabled on 737 with no other effect), mitv.service,
com.mi.bluetooth, com.droidlogic* (Amlogic system), com.xiaomi.gtv.settings.
